personal.name: Syed Burhan Ahmed
personal.title: AI Engineer, Researcher & Technical Mentor
personal.tagline: AI Engineer specializing in Computer Vision, Agentic Systems & Production ML
personal.bio: Building production-grade ML systems using Python, PyTorch, YOLOv11, FastAPI, LangChain, and n8n. Currently engineering an algorithmic trading bot, a conversational AI agent, and benchmarking VLMs against human baselines for my Final Year Capstone Project. IEEE Published Author (ICIC 2025).
personal.closingBio: Open to collaborating on challenging, impact-driven engineering problems. Whether it’s deployable computer vision systems, workflow automation infrastructures, or mentoring developers, the focus is on building reliable tech that solves real-world bottlenecks.
story: I am an AI Engineer building robust, production-grade systems across Computer Vision, Agentic AI, and applied ML. At OptimusFox, I'm simultaneously building an autonomous algorithmic trading bot with real-time signal generation, driving integration of a recommendation engine into BookItUp's backend, and architecting a conversational AI agent enabling full in-app flows through natural language.

In research at UMT's AVR Makerspace Lab, my FYP benchmarks closed-source vs. open-source VLMs — Gemma 4, Grounding DINO, CLIP, and Jina — against human baselines on real-world perception tasks including object counting, license plate recognition, and scene understanding, all on a constrained 16GB GPU. I also developed InsightVision, a FastAPI microservice orchestrating a hybrid YOLO/VLM pipeline achieving <100ms latency for semantic natural-language visual querying.

I published my first IEEE paper at ICIC 2025 on Vision-Based Fall Detection for Elderly Surveillance using YOLOv11 (DOI: 10.1109/ICIC68258.2025). Beyond engineering, I have trained 120+ participants as a Master Trainer in Generative AI and served as Teaching Assistant across three semesters covering Digital Logic Design and Introduction to Robotics.
